heroHeadline: "Tracking Bad Bunny" Wins Webby Award at 30th Annual Ceremony; European Tour Debuts in Barcelona in 11 Days; "DtMF" at 58 Weeks No. 1
heroSubtitle: Tracking the rise from SoundCloud uploads in Vega Baja to 100 billion Spotify streams, a historic Super Bowl LX halftime performance, and Grammy Album of the Year. On May 11, the 30th Annual Webby Awards ceremony at Cipriani Wall Street formally presented the juried Webby Award for Best Fan Engagement to the "Tracking Bad Bunny" location-based campaign by DDB Latina Puerto Rico — the first Webby tied to a Latin music release — completing the campaign's recognition cycle after nominations from Billboard, Variety, and Hollywood Reporter. The Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart dated May 9 confirms "DtMF" at 58 consecutive weeks at No. 1, further extending Bad Bunny's own all-time record beyond "Despacito" (56 weeks). The Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour's first-ever European stadium run opens May 22–23 at Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys in Barcelona (sold out), continuing to Lisbon, Madrid, and 11 countries through July.
footerNote: Data sourced from Rimas Entertainment, Billboard, Spotify Newsroom, RIAA, Latin Recording Academy, Recording Academy, Pollstar, Webby Awards, DDB Latina Puerto Rico, Adidas Newsroom, The Hollywood Reporter, Variety, Bloomberg, NPR, Remezcla, Deadline, Complex, Bleacher Report, Rolling Stone, Live Nation, Estadi Olímpic Barcelona, and major media
